Create Candidate Stratification Variables

Source: R/create_strata_functions.R
create_stratification_candidates.Rd

Generates a named list of candidate stratifications for use with compare_stratifications, compare_stratifications_precoding, and the sampling functions. By default this reproduces the earlier library (tertiles, quartiles, and quintiles of each variable plus 2x2, 2x3, 3x2, and 3x3 crossings of each pair of variables) with three changes: quantile cuts are made within each treatment arm when Z is supplied, categorical variables are also offered at their native levels, and every candidate is screened so that each stratum-by-arm cell holds at least min_cell_size units and no two candidates induce the same partition of the units. The library can be extended with other group counts and crossings, user-supplied cutpoints, and externally built stratifications.

create_stratification_candidates(
  dat,
  vars,
  Z = NULL,
  cut_by_arm = TRUE,
  n_groups = c(3, 4, 5),
  interaction_configs = c("2x2", "2x3", "3x2", "3x3"),
  breaks = NULL,
  custom = NULL,
  cross_levels = TRUE,
  cross_custom = TRUE,
  max_levels = 10,
  min_cell_size = 2,
  drop_duplicates = TRUE,
  jitter_vars = NULL,
  sd_jitter = 0.001,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

dat

Data frame containing the variables to stratify on.

vars

Character vector of column names in dat to build stratifications from.

Z

Optional name of the treatment indicator column in dat. When supplied, quantile cuts are made within each arm if cut_by_arm = TRUE, and the min_cell_size screen is applied to stratum-by-arm cells rather than to strata. Default NULL.

cut_by_arm

Logical. If TRUE (default) and Z is supplied, quantile breaks for continuous variables are computed separately within each treatment arm, so every arm is divided into equally sized strata and the labels denote within-arm quantile ranks ("Low Yhat" is the bottom tertile of predicted scores within the arm). If FALSE, breaks are computed on the pooled sample and define the same subgroups in both arms (needed, for example, for stratum-specific treatment effects). Categorical variables and breaks cuts are never cut by arm.

n_groups

Integer vector of group counts for single-variable quantile cuts. Default c(3, 4, 5).

interaction_configs

Pairwise quantile crossings, as strings such as "2x3" (first variable of the pair in 2 groups, second in 3) or as length-2 integer vectors. Default c("2x2", "2x3", "3x2", "3x3"). NULL suppresses quantile-by-quantile crossings.

breaks

Optional named list of numeric cutpoint vectors, one element per variable (names must be in vars), e.g. list(Yhat_raw = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9)). Give a named list of vectors to get several cuts of one variable, e.g. list(Yhat_raw = list(binned = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9), binned2 = c(0, 2, 3, 4, 9))). Cutpoints are fixed values applied identically in both arms.

custom

Optional named list of externally built stratifications (for example, embedding-cluster labels). Each element is a vector of length nrow(dat) or a function of dat returning one.

cross_levels

Logical; let native levels and breaks cuts enter pairwise crossings, with the quantile cuts of the other variable (at the group counts appearing in interaction_configs) and with each other. Default TRUE.

cross_custom

Logical; cross each custom stratification with every single-variable stratification of the variables in vars. Default TRUE.

max_levels

A variable that is a factor, character, or logical, or numeric with at most this many distinct values, is also offered at its native levels ({var}_levels). Default 10.

min_cell_size

Minimum number of units required in every cell of a candidate, where a cell is a stratum-by-arm combination when Z is supplied and a stratum otherwise. Candidates with any smaller cell, including a stratum that is empty in one arm, are dropped. Default 2, the smallest cell with an estimable within-cell variance; 0 disables the screen.

drop_duplicates

Logical; drop candidates that induce exactly the same partition of the units as an earlier candidate (for instance, the tertiles of a three-level variable duplicate its native levels). The first construction keeps its name; dropped ones are listed in the screening log. Default TRUE.

jitter_vars

Character vector (subset of vars) to which small random noise is added before computing quantile breaks, to break ties. Useful for integer-valued variables such as word counts, especially with cut_by_arm = TRUE. Default NULL.

sd_jitter

Standard deviation of the jitter noise. Default 1e-3.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility when jitter is applied. Default NULL.

verbose

Logical; print a one-line summary of how many candidates were constructed, kept, and dropped. Default TRUE.

Value

A named list of factors, each a candidate stratification of length nrow(dat), with a "screening" attribute: a tibble with one row per constructed candidate giving n_strata, the smallest cell (min_cell), whether it was kept, and the reason if not. Retrieve it with attr(candidates, "screening").

Details

Naming. Single-variable candidates are {var}_levels (native levels), {var}_cut or {var}_{name} (user cutpoints), and {var}_tertiles, {var}_quartiles, {var}_quintiles, or {var}_q{k} (quantile cuts). Pairwise crossings are {var1}_{var2}_{tag1}x{tag2}, where a tag is a group count, levels, or the name of a cut (for example Yhat_word_count_2x3 or Yhat_all_agree_3xlevels). Custom stratifications appear under their own names and, when crossed, as {custom}_x_{var}_{tag}.

Screening runs in construction order (native levels and user cuts, then quantile cuts, then custom stratifications, then crossings that involve levels or cuts, then quantile crossings), so when two candidates coincide the more descriptive name survives. Candidates whose construction fails (non-unique quantile breaks in the pooled sample or in either arm, too few distinct values), that contain missing values, or that have fewer than two strata are dropped and logged as well.

The min_cell_size screen is a necessary condition only: it guarantees that within-cell variances exist, not that they are well estimated. For pilot-based allocation, filter further on min_stratum_size in the comparison tables.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Default library, cut within arm and screened
cands <- create_stratification_candidates(dat, vars = c("Yhat", "word_count"), Z = "Z")
attr(cands, "screening")

# READS-style library: rubric bins of the raw score, crossed with LLM
# agreement, plus an external clustering
cands <- create_stratification_candidates(
    dat, vars = c("Yhat", "Yhat_raw", "n_distinct_Yhat", "all_agree"), Z = "Z",
    breaks = list(Yhat_raw = list(binned = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9),
                                  binned2 = c(0, 2, 3, 4, 9))),
    custom = list(embed_k6 = dat$embedding_cluster) )
} # }
